source_title: On Arratia's coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
title: The law of Arratia's random integer J_x^*: P[J_x^* = j] = (1/(j log x))(1 + O(1/log x))

statement_spans.label: Lemma lem:probaj (Arratia): law of the random integer J_x^* built from the transformed Poisson process

proof_spans.label: complete author proof: Poisson prime-power counts, Dirichlet-series inversion, Mecke expansion, Mertens partial summation and the zeta expansion at t = 0

standard_prerequisites.name: Poisson process calculus on a product space
standard_prerequisites.reference: source 1795-1852, quoted from Kingman 2.3, 3.2, 5.1 and Last-Penrose Th. 4.5; process R at 678-698
standard_prerequisites.statement: R has intensity exp(-wy) dw dy; with S_i = sum_{l>=i} Y_l the process {S_i} is Poisson of intensity ds/s; the Mecke equation evaluates sums over distinct Poisson points.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies R^*, its labelling, and the Mecke identity that converts the indicator of {J_x^* = j} into an integral. The spacing lemma is quoted, not reproved.

standard_prerequisites.name: Chebyshev function and Mertens estimate
standard_prerequisites.reference: source 429-431 and the quoted Mertens estimate at 788 (Koukoulopoulos Th. 3.4(a))
standard_prerequisites.statement: theta(x) = sum_{p<=x} log p, Lambda is von Mangoldt, and sum_{q<=u} Lambda(q)/q = log u + O(1).
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the prime-power tail in the Mecke integral into an explicit asymptotic in t.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dirichlet series of a multiplicative Poisson product
standard_prerequisites.statement: For N_q(t) Poisson of parameter Lambda(q)/(q^{1+t} log q) and I_t^* = prod_q q^{N_q(t)}, one has E[(I_t^*)^{-s}] = zeta(1+t+s)/zeta(1+t).

core_obligations: Fix the labelling (T_i^*, Q_i^*) of R^* and J_x^* = prod_{i=1}^K Q_i^* with prod_{i=1}^K Q_i^* <= x < prod_{i=0}^K Q_i^* (source 752-760).
Compute the law of I_t^* from the Poisson parameters and read off P[I_t^* = i] = i^{-1-t}/zeta(1+t) (774-778).
Write the indicator of {J_x^* = j} as a sum over Poisson points with I^*_{T^*} = j and Q^* > x/j, and evaluate it with the Mecke equation (778-787).

Estimate the integral: Mertens plus partial summation give sum_{q>x/j} Lambda(q)/q^{1+t} = (x/j)^{-t}(1+O(t))/t, and the split at t = 1 with 1/zeta(1+t) = t + O(t^2) yields 1/(j log x)(1+O(1/log x)) (788-800).

proof_roadmap.step: Introduce N_q(t) and I_t^*, obtain the Dirichlet-series identity, and use the Mecke equation to write P[J_x^* = j] as the integral (eq:probaJ).
Apply Mertens plus partial summation to the prime-power tail and substitute into (eq:probaJ).
Split the t-integral at 1, use zeta(1+t) >= 1 for t >= 1 and 1/zeta(1+t) = t + O(t^2) on (0,1], and evaluate the remaining elementary integral.

difficulty_reason: The claim pins down the exact law of Arratia's random integer J_x^* = prod_{i=1}^K Q_i^*, built from the transformed Poisson process R^*, up to relative error O(1/log x). The proof does not estimate P[J_x^* = j] by inclusion-exclusion: it first identifies the law of the partial product I_t^* from the Dirichlet series prod_q exp((Lambda(q)/(q^{1+t} log q))(q^{-s} - 1)) = zeta(1+t+s)/zeta(1+t), which forces P[I_t^* = i] = i^{-1-t}/zeta(1+t) (source 774-778), and then writes the indicator of {J_x^* = j} as a sum over Poisson points with Q^* > x/j and evaluates it with the Mecke equation (778-787). The remaining step is a genuine asymptotic in t: Mertens plus partial summation give sum_{q>x/j} Lambda(q)/q^{1+t} = (x/j)^{-t}(1+O(t))/t, and the split at t = 1 using 1/zeta(1+t) = t + O(t^2) produces the main term 1/(j log x) (788-800).

dedup.scope: Targeted neighbours only: the public identity index for the fixed JEP 12 (2025) 1565-1604 source, the two same-source prepared cards, the 400 retired claims and the probability scouting notes for source 2516.

compared.actual_statement: source 200-207: existence of a coupling of the uniform random integer N_x with a parameter-one Poisson-Dirichlet process whose expected total l1 discrepancy is of order 1
compared.difference: The new claim is a distributional identity for the auxiliary integer J_x^* inside Arratia's coupling with relative error O(1/log x); it states no coupling of N_x with V and bounds no l1 discrepancy, and its proof (774-800) shares no span with 200-207.

That card estimates a Dirichlet boundary event whose radius depends on the same Poisson-Dirichlet sequence, via beta localization and a two-point Mecke argument at 1448-1628. Here a point probability of one integer-valued statistic is bounded; the Mecke use is the one-point expansion at 782-787 and the conclusion is a logarithmic relative error, not a boundary-event probability.

That card sums over multiplicative k-factorizations with a square-full/square-free decomposition and hyperbola sums at 1370-1446; the new claim concerns the law of J_x^* alone and needs only a single prime-power tail.

editorial_notes: The claim is Arratia's Lemma 2 as restated by the authors, who supply their own proof at 773-801; the attribution stays in the lemma heading.
The Mecke equation is quoted from Last-Penrose at 1845-1852 and is applied to a nonnegative summand, exactly the range of the quoted statement.
The following section 803-1113 on the event {J_x != J_x^*} and the total variation distance is not included and is not used by this proof.
All displayed estimates are taken from the fixed publisher source unchanged.
